title: Level 3 (Advanced) - B-9
notes:
West leads the ♥K against 2♠. The defense starts by taking the first 4 tricks (2 heart tricks and 2 diamond tricks) before declarer gains the lead. South still must lose a trick to the ♣A. South must avoid losing a trump trick. The ♠Q must be found.

South can decide which opponent to finesse for the ♠Q by playing on clubs first. The defender who holds the ♣A cannot hold the ♠Q. So far both defenders are known to have started with 7 high card points (West the ♥A and ♥K, East the ♦A and ♦K).

Whoever has the ♣A has 11 high card points. As both opponents passed when they could have opened the bidding, the defender with the ♣A can't have the ♠Q. That would give him 13 high card points and a certain opening bid. When West shows up with the ♣A, East should later be finessed for the ♠Q.
